paragraphs: Lena said she'd donate three pints to me herself, because with this … vibe-coding I only started seeing her when a beer appeared in my hand, and now I just stare at the computer and have come to resemble the most pointless piece of furniture, because you can't even put a vase of flowers on me)
There's a theory that gaylord Altman created vibe-coding in order to … all the front-wheel-drives.
First we wean them off undesirable interaction with the opposite sex, and then we release an update in which they…
Damn, in short, I kept trying to understand what's off with the arrival of 5.6 Sol. Something changed, but I couldn't understand what.
And now I've got it:

The model now does tasks far wider and deeper, one prompt instead of 10-30-50, and it hammers away far faster than that constellation, but still 3–6 hours. And you can't run many sessions. And the demand on cognitive load has dropped significantly.

But the habit had formed, and now it's somehow uncomfortable that you're thinking with the former density, and that much isn't needed anymore. There's simply nowhere to put these tasks and prompts, and vibe-coding into notes for the drawer is somehow painful.
Which means… having loaded Codex up for great deeds, you can PLAY DOTA.
This thought excited me so much that sweat broke out on my temples.
Now I sit here embarrassed by this thought, chewing the edge of my lip, fiddling with the hem of my T-shirt.
I've got one task that's been running on Ultracode for 35 hours now)
I'm afraid to imagine how many times a compact happened in there)
But progress is going in an amazing way
Every time I think about stopping it, I read the telemetry, and there are sensible thoughts there and something has moved 5 cm somewhere))
Now it's even interesting purely out of the research spirit:
A) will it finish or not
B) will I have to redo things, what and how much)
But generally Ultracode is scary to press
It takes several times longer than just setting the task on Max
In general I'm sure Ultracode is some experimental ….
Roughly like /goal
The task is complex, but an 8-hour one, not 38
Ultracode is clearly misfiring somewhere, looping, grinding idly for a very long time where the amount of code ultimately required is incomparably small
Probably because many smart agents each latch onto too many details, and then all of it has to somehow be reconciled among them, and no context window is enough for such a multitude
My task says it has already changed 280+ files
A compact … every three messages in the telemetry
I think much of what it's tormenting there would have been done 100 times faster and better separately
The models have become smarter than their context window. Kind of like a very brave animal with a very weak body
Haha, decided to try using the GPT PRO in the chat they built into Codex.

It turned out to be an ultra-cool thing. Essentially you design with this GPT PRO, and when you're already completely, completely sure of yourself, and GPT PRO has prepared, besides the context, the entire task for 5.6 Sol Max, you press a button and the whole context from the conversation with GPT PRO flies off as essentially a task for 5.6 Sol Max in Codex to work through.

Still clumsy as … compared to if we simply set the task to GPT PRO in Codex and it decided by itself which models would do what, but better than before, when there was no connection at all and you had to generate the notional prompt packs with Pro and deliver them to Codex in your beak.

HOWEVER, I don't even know how to feel about this, but GPT PRO 5.6 has of course become smarter than 5.5, and it doesn't just boggle the imagination but also…. the first document it wrote as the KICK-OFF of our design was 8,600 words, or ~1,200 lines of an .md file.

And it wasn't a throwaway wall of text. Honestly — it was an absolutely brilliant text you could take right now to some Mann-Ivanov-Ferber and publish as a book, and nobody would ever in their life guess that it's … not a book.
In the end I read the damn thing and answered Pro's 16 open, … detailed questions; that took me an hour and a half that I'd thought I'd sleep through, but I quite often get my hopes up in life.

Pro then contentedly started chewing what I'd returned to it, and says to me: well, brother, you told me everything just right, now I'll write you a plan of……………. 28–30 thousand words. And you and I will discuss it.
If you were planning to finally relax with all these new … LLMs, I have bad news for you =)))))))
In ordinary modern typesetting 30 thousand words is 100–130 pages, depending on the canvas size, typeface and print quality…
I'm …
Why the …!!!!!!!!
So that's what doing something all your life is like, apparently.
It just seemed to me that everything I do is … from under a horse. These … sales. … to discuss and do there.

But now, over these six months, it's as if I've been able to touch the real volumes of this skill, which are simply inaccessible to salespeople who don't do this kind of methodologistics, for the reason that “it's not even clear where to look at this skill in such a form.”

I'm just designing a small … — market research in PREPARATION for launching sales mailings. And I've already read 8,000 words from which 30,000 words are born, and this is all still only PREPARATION, … piss in my ear.

And folks, though I'm tired, I'm in my right mind. There really wasn't a single superfluous word in those 8,000. Moreover, they were compressed as much as an LLM can. So why does the brain shrivel all this down to the elementary and seemingly always visible inside the head as if in the palm of your hand? … you … … brain, I'll screw you myself
Haha, been a while now, man
And it's striking how unlimited it is there
For Ultima I generated 160 images with one prompt that Claude Design wrote for me

In general I now use Claude Design like this: I tell it, like, think through the design with beautiful raster images in mind, switch on your imagination, and tell me what to order from Codex so you can assemble from it a truly unique and … site
Give me exact sizes, styles, basically everything you ask for, Codex will do exactly as you need
Claude Design ends up imagining some layout and gives you a prompt for X images to Codex
Codex makes them FROM ONE PROMPT
And lays them out as Claude Design asked
You bring it back and voilà — it assembles the site with all the images Codex generated)
For example my Ultima installer was made exactly this way
Meaning this was possible back in ~March =)
So, … coders who are typing their Santa Barbara at me in DMs following the drama that unfolded in the chat — GO ….
Some of you mistakenly thought I'm interested in listening to your opinion about how hard life really is for coders, and how unfair I am to you. … GO ….

You're distracting me from matters far more important than your … experiences that NOBODY GIVES A DAMN ABOUT. If I write in the channel or in the group, believe me, I do it not for you but for myself. Express your opinion or emotions about it in the group to each other, send money to the card, … I don't know, go to Antarctica and piss a yellow stream there on snow packed down by harsh southern winds. But don't type this … at me in DMs!!!! Every time you feel like doing that, pause your life to try to determine which direction the … is in right now, and trudge in that direction.
Seriously, now unknown long-haired … are going to mumble at me about things expressible in the smallest prime numbers, and I'm supposed to sit and listen to this ….
You really found your time in a dumpster, apparently =(((
Better bring me cash, … recommendations for vibe-coders, a wonderful mood and boundless blessings!!!
… in short, I realized that on one hand I'm glad the neural nets are getting smarter, but on the other I'm puzzled and frightened. And the second more than the first.
The thing is that before, when a new neural net came out, you had to adapt, but it was adaptation in terms of prompting, working with project memory, the sequence and method of setting tasks, etc.
But… all of that was, like, on a subtle level.
Overall the mechanism didn't change from GPT 5 to GPT 5.5 — you want to work on something, you prompt in loops, you prompt one-offs, you prompt … diagonally, you turn to GPT PRO, and off you go.
Not everything was done easily. Not everything was done quickly. But the iterations were fast, and you could correct your direction. The skill grew, and the feeling of control grew.
Now I've lost the feeling of control. And what's frightening is that it's even in a repo where the feeling of control used to be absolute, earned over these many months.
And the feeling was lost against the length of the iterations GPT in Codex now works with.

Fable has … gone off entirely. It just switches to Opus right away, so in the world of subscriptions I personally consider that outside Claude Design it simply no longer exists, until someone proves otherwise.
GPT, on the other hand, exists, but… First, I can no longer predict how long it will work on a task. AT ALL.
Right now GPT 5.6 Sol Max (without Ultra) has been working on one task of mine for about 32 hours.
There was a time Sol … for more than 40 hours.
Before, I understood that a task would take from 30 minutes to, well, a MAXIMUM of 5 hours. On average 1.5 for ultra-complex tasks on an ultra-gigantic repo.
Now I can't predict anything anymore and that's frightening.

It's frightening also because I no longer understand how to plan my day. At the stage when your repo already brings you money and you're only doing improvements, that's probably less damage. Even so, you need to promise something to someone, but you can't. Before, I could tell a client precisely: I'll fix this in a couple of hours. And even if I didn't make it, it was TODAY.

Now I don't know what to answer at all. Maybe today, maybe by the end of the month, …. Because although GPT has become a hundred times smarter, I wouldn't claim it understands me the way I understand myself, or that it one-shots tasks.
Meaning it may randomly work for 2 days on a … that would previously have taken me 3 hours, and after that I still don't know whether I'll have to throw in the next prompt on the same task or not.
It's already happened several times, and a thing that seemed elementary to me it … for another 11 hours. Thank God it finished successfully.
But that's not vibe-coding anymore.

And I'm practically certain, guys, that there's actually no need for this at all. I mean — I clearly understand it's a fiction, a paradigm shift, saving on inference, whatever — but not a technological limitation.
Today, before my eyes, on several tasks in the THIRD HOUR of work, the model made fewer than 68 lines of edits to the repo's code.

So what the … was it doing there? There were no multi-level requests to other neural nets. There was no … knows what deep research. This was a task precisely about development. In the end, in the 16th hour, I see it has touched 56 files and….. added +2,441 lines of code =)))
But 5.5 could add +5,000 lines of code in 15 minutes for … .

Actually I'm now one last evening away from stopping using the new models, and starting to use them only if I'm in despair for some reason, although I can't imagine why I'd end up in it. On 5.5 I wasn't in despair once in the last two months. I just coded and that's it. And everything developed wonderfully.

Over the course of today I couldn't add a single task, and I've already switched subscriptions twice. So the third weekly limit has gone in a day, on two sessions that so far have produced less code than I used to produce in ~5 hours in four 5.5 sessions.

I need to go light a candle against … FOMO. Because that's exactly what's screaming in both ears: … you don't understand something, you're a sucker, go … yourself, sit and use 5.6 Sol, you dog. You're a dog, suck, this is animality. Obey the master. Love Fable, love 5.6, don't love your mom anymore, go enlist in the army, go and die for the real guys. You're not a real guy. This is not real.
